notes:
Canonical basic-turn for copilot: one user prompt, one text-only assistant reply, no tool use, asserting the ready→working→ready arc plus non-zero tokens. Recorded with the INTERACTIVE driver — the REPL must outlive the daemon's observation window or the settle to ready is never seen. PRESESSION SHAPE (provisional, from code): copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch holding only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt, so processlifecycle.Scanner mints a proc-<PID> row (1s poll) before the fswatcher can see any transcript; the real session then arrives under a DIFFERENT id. Birth is therefore modeled as two phases and every post-birth phase is anchored to the REAL session, templated from the codex/mistral-vibe siblings. first_turn_end anchors to first_turn_start (not session_birth) so the matcher picks the post-turn ready rather than the birth ready. OBSERVATIONS: tokens and cost are both live from assistant.message.outputTokens through the shared capacity price map (session.usage_checkpoint carries no token counts at all — only shutdown does), so tokens_nonzero and cost_nonzero are both asserted. model is NOT pinned: --model accepts only "auto" on this account and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn, so an exact match would be nondeterministic.

BIRTH RE-ANCHORED 2026-08-03: the real session is born directly into `working`, not `ready`. copilot writes events.jsonl only when the first prompt is sent, so at discovery the file ALREADY holds the open turn; since commit 3cde4f8d ("fix(detector): classify every new session against its own metrics, not just children") buildNewSessionState classifies that birth against its own metrics instead of hard-coding StateReady. Recording 2026-08-03-17-47-42 shows state_transition(new session created) landing new_state=working on the real session. The transient proc-<PID> row is still born ready and remains the presession_birth anchor. The pre-fix spec asserted a ready birth for the real session followed by a separate ready→working; that shape was the bug the fix removed, so session_birth and first_turn_start are now ONE phase.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)
The real <session-id> session reconciles under a different session id once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt, and is born DIRECTLY into working because the file already holds the open turn
